title: How to Do a Knee Push-Up for Beginners
intro: The knee push-up is the best step for beginners who can't do a full push-up yet. It still trains the same muscles, just with a lighter load.
muscles: Chest, front shoulders, back of the arms (triceps) and core. Honest note: this exercise strengthens your arms, but it doesn't specifically remove arm fat. That comes from your overall eating and movement.
steps: Kneel on a mat or towel, hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders.
Move your knees back until your body is straight from head to knees.
Tighten your tummy and glutes, don't let your bum stick up.
Bend your elbows back and lower your chest towards the floor.
Push the floor to come back up while breathing out.
mistakes: Bum sticking up, body in a 'V' shape. This reduces the work for your chest. Straighten your hips.
Knees too close to your hands. Move your knees further back so your body is angled and straight.
Elbows flaring out too wide. Bring them in a bit, about 45 degrees from your body.
easier: Do wall push-ups or push-ups with your hands on the kitchen table.
harder: Lower slowly for 3-4 seconds. Then try full push-ups with your hands on a sofa, or lower slowly from a full push-up position (negatives) and come up on your knees.
dose: 2-3 sets x 6-12 reps, rest 60 seconds. Do it 2-3 times a week.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your shoulders, wrists or knees. If the pain continues, see a doctor or physiotherapist.

faq.a: They count! They train the same muscles as full push-ups. Many people build strength with knee push-ups first before moving up a level.

faq.q: When can I switch to full push-ups?
faq.a: When you can do 3 sets x 12-15 knee push-ups with clean technique. Start with 1-3 full push-ups, then finish the set with knee push-ups.

faq.q: My knees hurt when pressing on the floor. What should I do?
faq.a: Put a folded towel, thin pillow or yoga mat under your knees. If the pain comes from inside the knee, not because of the hard floor, switch to wall push-ups and get advice from a physio.
